waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-17 re-audit after the county's per-site pages tagged 'Lakefront: Yes'. Langlade County Konect Parks pages (langladeforestryandparks.com/parks/camping/jack_lake_campground__cabins/site_N/, read 2026-11-17): sites 7-15 and 50-57 'Lakefront: Yes' (6, 16, 49 'No'); 7-15 'All sites are wooded and shaded with a gravel base', 45x35 to 70x32 ft; 52-57 'Situated on the South Shore of Jack Lake' (35x20 to 61x37 ft, no photos posted). All sold by the night, online reservation only ($45 electric / $40 sites 49-57 'All Days'). Official site photos (site_7..15, rendered): every pad in mature hardwood with brush between pad and shore; the lake shows through the trees from 9 (picnic table at the pad end, water ~20-30 m beyond through trunks), 13 and 14 (water behind the parked trailer through trees), faintly 12; no pad has open ground to the water. Campground map (updated_campground_map2.jpeg): 9-15 on the outside of the north loop facing the lake, 7-8 on its east side, 51-57 on the south shore of the east bay, 50 set back inland. Esri World Imagery (leaf-off; Wayback names 2017-05-08 WV02 0.5 m) 900, 400, 200 and 220 m frames, all rendered: north loop road ~36-40 m and east loop road ~40 m from the shore, pads between road and water under bare deciduous canopy with an evergreen/brush fringe ~10-20 m deep along the whole shoreline; south-shore area = a mowed clearing with fire rings whose north edge is ~27-34 m from the water behind a continuous tree belt, a footpath (~37 m) from its NW corner to a small landing. USGS NAIP 2022-06-23 0.6 m (leaf-on, rendered): continuous canopy from the main loop to the waterline; campers on the south-shore clearing, tree belt intact between it and the bay. No pad has open unscreened ground to the water within ~50 m, so no lakefront despite the county tag; filtered views from 9, 12-14 in the official photos earn lakeview. Natural lake, no dam. --Claude
note: Langlade County campground on Jack Lake northeast of Antigo, in mature maple, birch, oak and pine beside Veterans Memorial Park (beach, playground, disc golf). Direct access to the Ice Age Trail, mountain-bike and ski trails, and the county ATV/UTV and snowmobile trails. Sites 7-15 back onto the wooded shore with the lake seen through the trees; 51-57 sit on a clearing behind a belt of trees on the south shore, with a footpath to the water. 49-57 (the former South Shore area) take one camping unit and no tents. Three sleeping cabins. --Claude
reasons: County 'Lakefront: Yes' sites 7-15/50-57 are wooded pads behind a shoreline tree belt (photos + leaf-off Esri + NAIP 2022); water visible through trees from 9, 12-14 -> lakeview, not lakefront
